bib.title: Large Language Models are Effective Text Rankers with Pairwise Ranking Prompting

read.skipped: References skimmed only. PDF is arXiv v2, 28 Mar 2024; no venue printed.

question: Can off-the-shelf moderate-sized open-source LLMs rank documents competitively with fine-tuned rankers and giant blackbox LLMs if the prompt is reduced to a pairwise comparison?
hypothesis: Pointwise and listwise ranking prompts are too hard for off-the-shelf LLMs; a pairwise comparison is simpler, needs no calibration, and should work much better.
contributions: First published demonstration of pairwise ranking prompting (PRP) effectiveness for ranking with LLMs, with state-of-the-art performance on a wide range of datasets using simple prompting and scoring.
Results use moderate-sized open-source LLMs, compared with solutions using blackbox, commercial, larger models.
Study of several efficiency improvements (Allpair, Sorting, Sliding window) with promising empirical performance.

method.summary: A pairwise prompt asks the LLM which of two passages is more relevant to a query. Each pair is queried in both orders; consistent answers give a local order, inconsistent ones a tie. Three aggregations are used: all-pairs win counting (O(N^2)), heapsort with the LLM as comparator (O(N log N)), and K bubble-sort-like sliding passes (O(N) each). Reranks BM25 top-100 with no fine-tuning.

datasets.name: TREC-DL2019
datasets.source: MS MARCO v1 passage corpus, 8.8 million passages; dense human relevance annotations
datasets.preprocessing: Rerank top 100 passages retrieved by BM25 (Pyserini, Lin et al. 2021) per query

datasets.source: MS MARCO v1 passage corpus, 8.8 million passages

inference.decoding: Main results use scoring mode: log-likelihood of target text 'Passage A' / 'Passage B' given the prompt; generation mode compared in Table 5
inference.samples: Each pair queried twice (both orders). Single run per method; no seeds or variance reported.
inference.prompting: Zero-shot, single pairwise template, identical for all 9 datasets; no demonstrations
inference.retrieval: BM25 top-100 per query as initial ranking; BM25 order resolves ties, prediction conflicts and failures

parameters.PRP-Sliding-K: K=10 passes in main results; passes run backward (from lowest BM25 rank) with stride 1; ablation 1/2/3/10 backward and 1 forward
parameters.PRP-Allpair score: s_i = 1*sum_{j!=i} I[d_i>d_j] + 0.5*sum_{j!=i} I[d_i=d_j]; ties fall back to initial ranking
parameters.PRP-Sorting: Heapsort, O(N log N), comparator = PRP unit
parameters.consistency rule: d1>d2 or d2>d1 only if both orderings agree, else d1=d2

other.complexity: Allpair O(N^2) calls (parallelisable), Sorting O(N log N), Sliding O(N) per pass

metrics.name: NDCG@1, NDCG@5, NDCG@10
metrics.definition: Normalised discounted cumulative gain at cut-off k on the reranked top 100

eval.protocol: Single run per configuration; no significance tests or variance. LLM baselines from other papers are copied (RankGPT, LRL); all unsupervised LLM methods use BM25 order to resolve conflicts.

availability.weights: FLAN-T5 and FLAN-UL2 are open; text-bison is blackbox
availability.data: Plans to release pairwise inference results (JSON with ids, text, label, retrieval rank and score, prompt, generated text, score) on 9 datasets and 3 open models; not released at time of the paper ('plan to release')

limits: No GPT models are run by the authors; GPT numbers are copied from other papers (Limitations).
Focus is empirical; PRP-Sorting does not guarantee transitivity and theoretically grounded noisy-sorting methods are left for future work.
Possible data leakage cannot be excluded: FLAN has an MS MARCO question-answering task; blackbox LLM training data is unknown (Appendix C). Authors avoid the word 'zero-shot'.
Only relevance-style ranking tested; non-standard ranking such as ArguAna counter-arguments untested (Appendix C).
PRP-Allpair is O(N^2) calls; cost, latency and wall-clock are never reported. Sliding-K depends on input order (Table 4).
No seeds, variance, or significance tests; temperature and hardware not stated; code not released at time of writing (only 'plan to release' data).
Only BM25 top-100 reranking tested; PRP-Sliding-10 needs at most 10 passes so only the top-10 is reliably sorted.
Comparisons are against baseline numbers from other papers whose GPT versions are now dated; gpt-4 result used as reference.

terms.definition: Prompt with the query and a pair of documents for the LLM to say which is more relevant
Enumerates all pairs and aggregates a win-count score per document; O(N^2) calls
Uses LLM pairwise preferences as the comparator for Heapsort; O(N log N)
K passes of bubble-sort-like compare-and-swap with stride 1 from bottom of list; O(N) per pass

figures.caption: Two existing prompting methods for ranking: (a) the pointwise relevance generation approach and (b) the listwise permutation approach.
figures.why: Shows the two baseline prompt formats PRP replaces.

figures.caption: An illustration of pairwise ranking prompting. The scores in scoring mode represent the log-likelihood of the model generating the target text given the prompt.
figures.why: Shows generation mode vs scoring mode with the same prompt.

figures.caption: An illustration of one pass of our sliding window approach. Starting from right to left, we compare each document pair and swap it if the LLM output disagrees with the initial ranking. K such passes will ensure a high-performing top-K ranking.
figures.why: Shows the bubble-sort-like pass faster than prose.

figures.caption: Comparison of pointwise, listwise, and pairwise approaches.
figures.why: Compares API calls, generation vs scoring API support and calibration needs.
